messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate on hosted-prod. Rolling 5m error rate = 18%. Initial spike at 2026-03-15T02:00Z. Severity: P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/2750001234
Maya: acked. I'm oncall but wrapping up a shift. quick handoff note below. :wave:
Raul: copying. are you still primary or should i take over now?
Maya: I'm primary until 02:15Z (15 min). I'll walk through what I have so far:
Maya: - Symptoms: increased 5xx on hostpool-hosted-1, mostly INTERNAL_ERROR (500) and some 503s
Maya: - Short term mitigation attempted: scaled pool by +2 nodes (no change), disabled recent rollout of model-id: redwood-13b-v2-quant
Maya: - Observations: latency spike precedes errors by ~3s, KV-cache miss rate up 30%
Kai: quick question — that rollout you disabled, did you pin traffic away or kill the deploy?
Maya: I rolled back the canary and pinned traffic to redwood-13b-v1. Canary instances are stopped.
Lina: FYI I see related warnings in infra metrics: kube-scheduler showing evictions on node-gpu-17 around 01:58Z
Raul: OK i'll take primary at 02:15Z. Kai you'll be secondary?
Kai: I can be secondary for the next 4 hours.
Maya: Handoff checklist (short):
- Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.example/runbooks/serve-high-5xx
- Key commands:
```
# tail recent logs for the model service
kubectl -n production logs -l app=serve -c model --since=10m | tail -n 200
# check node pressure
kubectl describe node node-gpu-17 | egrep -i "Eviction|Pressure"
```
Maya: If you need the customer-impact template, use /templates/hosted-5xx on support wiki.
Jordan (support-oncall): can confirm template exists. I can send out an initial heads-up to affected orgs if you tell me scope (tenant ids).
Raul: I'll gather tenant ids in 5m. Jordan, please be ready.
Priya (security-oncall): quick note — if we see any anomalous authentication errors or service account token errors, page security. For general 5xx without auth signs, security can standby.
Raul: question for the group: routing matrix — who do we page for what? I'm writing it down: runtime (model crashes/KV-cache logic) -> eng-runtime; infra (node pressure, kube evictions, autoscaler) -> eng-infra; security (auth/session/tokens/permissions) -> security-oncall; support -> support-oncall for customer comms. agree?
Alex (eng-platform): agree, but add eng-platform for capacity/fleet scaling/pools and dedicated capacity adjustments. Example: if we need to reassign GPUs across pools, page eng-platform.
Maya: +1 to Alex. Also if metrics/observability alerts look wrong (missing tags, bad ingestion) page eng-sre.
Raul: noted. I'll page eng-infra (oncall) for the node evictions and eng-platform for capacity shuffle.
Kai: quick triage step: check model-level OOMs and nvml errors on the node:
```
nvidia-smi -q | egrep -i "Error|Fail"
journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | grep -i oom
```
Lina: i'm watching the autoscaler dashboard, pods are stuck pending due to insufficient nvidia.com/gpu resource on us-west-2a.
Raul: is there a known coverage gap overnight for eng-infra? I remember a 03:00-05:00 UTC thin window last month.
Alex (eng-platform): yes, there's a partial coverage gap 03:00-04:00 UTC for senior infra oncall this week (holiday rota). We have oncall juniors but escalate path is slower.
Maya: that's important — if this goes long and needs infra escalation in that gap, escalate to eng-platform so they can trigger cloud provider quota increases.
Jordan (support-oncall): heads-up — if we need to send customer comms during the gap, I can draft and queue them; but approvals might be slower.
Priya (security-oncall): also flag — if any cross-tenant data exposure is suspected, immediate page to security regardless of time.
Raul: OK action items for my takeover:
- page eng-infra with node-gpu-17 eviction logs and link to incident
- page eng-platform for capacity/rollback assist (possible pool shuffle)
- gather tenant ids and prepare support template (Jordan)
- continue rollback verification and check KV-cache metrics
Maya: leaving one more note: if KV-cache miss rate stays high, consider toggling prefix caching OFF for the hot model as a temporary mitigation (runbook step 4).
Kai: noted. I'll check kv-store latencies and redis errors: `redis-cli -h kv-host latency latest`
incidence-bot: [UPDATE] Alert reassessed at 02:08Z — error rate held at 17%. Auto-snooze will trigger in 10m if no escalation.
Raul: paging eng-infra-now -> @eng-infra-oncall: node-gpu-17 evictions causing pod restarts, link https://incidents.redwood.example/2750001234 logs attached
Alex (eng-platform): I'm available to help with pool moves from 03:30-04:30Z if needed. Might cover the worst of the gap.
Lina: infra replied in channel, looking now.
Jordan (support-oncall): prep done. send me tenant list and I'll push the first broadcast template.
Raul: tenant list posted to incident doc. Jordan please proceed when ready.
Maya: one final: if you escalate to provider (quota/spot preemption), use the 'provider-escalation' runbook steps 2-5 and include incident id in ticket.
Raul: taking primary now. Maya thanks for the handoff. I'll post updates every 10 min. :thumbsup:
Maya: good luck, ping me if you want a quick sync later.
Priya (security-oncall): standing by for any auth anomalies.
incident-bot: [NOTE] Thread locked for updates — please keep messages compact and tag relevant oncall groups.
Raul: logging first status update at 02:20Z: errors steady, infra looking at node pressure, eng-platform standing by for capacity moves.
